question: What did sponsors do with companies like Punctual Pros?
html:
Sponsors that sold home-services companies like Punctual Pros for more mostly did six things in roughly the same order. They installed operators, bought early and nearby, kept a steady tuck-in cadence, ran one system, built memberships and owned technician hiring (value creation cases; Home-services company case studies).

The common sequence

  • Operators at entry. Alpine named Apex's CEO and CFO on launch day in July 2019. American Capital gave Service Experts' returning CEO about 10% ownership. Huron recruited Sciens' CEO before buying anything (value creation cases).
  • First add-on early and close. The median was about 7 months after entry across 11 dated cases. Smith + Howard did its first in month 9 (value creation cases).
  • Steady tuck-ins. The pace was roughly one every three to five months:
  • TurnPoint did 16 while revenue grew nearly 10x.
  • Sciens did 13.
  • BSP did nine at Smith + Howard as headcount went from ~100 to ~800 (value creation cases).
  • One system. Service Champions ran a single IT system with consolidated purchasing. Wrench books online at 99% of locations on ServiceTitan (Home-services company case studies).
  • Recurring revenue. Champions grew from ~60,000 members in 2021 to ~150,000 in 2026 and sold to Blackstone at a reported ~18.5x. That multiple is a press estimate (value creation cases).
  • Technician pipeline. Examples include Horizon's training center, Apex's academies and Sila's 2026 academy purchase (Home-services company case studies).

What went wrong elsewhere

  • Horizon was lender-owned by 2026. Any Hour carries PIK debt and is marked at 89. TurnPoint carries PIK debt and changed CEO.
  • In each case, brand count grew faster than integration (Home-services company case studies).
  • Few sponsors disclose entry or exit value, EBITDA or MOIC. Returns by lever cannot be compared directly (value creation cases).

Punctual Pros against the sequence

Punctual Pros is about 30 months past its Apr 3, 2024 entry (BSP firm profile; value creation cases).

LeverPunctual Pros status
Operator teamFounder CEO in place; integrator COO is the next step in the sequence (Home-services company case studies)
First add-onHorvath in month 8, in line with the median
Tuck-in cadenceBehind: only one add-on so far; 61-company target screen built (Punctual Pros nationwide plan)
One systemServiceTitan since September 2024
Memberships~6,500 members, est. (Punctual Pros nationwide plan)
Technician pipelineNo data in context

The nationwide plan's roadmap reaches ~$100M revenue and ~32,000 members by month 36. That roadmap is an est. built on assumptions, not a forecast (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

Next actions

  • Write the integrator COO role and start the search. Sequence this hire ahead of any increase in deal pace.
  • Rank the 61-company screen and set a target of one close every three to five months. Start with contiguous Central-PA and Maryland zip codes.
  • Pull actual member counts, churn and members per technician from ServiceTitan. These replace the ~6,500 est. and allow a benchmark against Champions' ~83 per technician.
  • Gather technician hiring sources, time-to-productivity and turnover data. These answer whether a training academy is warranted.
